history.rationale: D397 lies in a transmembrane helix and may participate in cation coordination; neutralization to alanine should impair transport while maintaining folding.
No new evidence this round; retained as the leading candidate given the charged-residue-to-alanine disruption rationale.

No new evidence this round; retained as a strong candidate for eliminating a negatively charged side chain likely involved in transport.
High alphamissense pathogenicity (0.845) strongly supports LOF transport ablation; moderate MSA tolerance (0.241) suggests some evolutionary acceptance, despite low ESM. Retained as top candidate.
Strong phenotype (0.845) and highest evolutionary conservation among candidates; functional annotation uninformative.
Tryptophan 216 is an aromatic residue in a hydrophobic stretch, potentially lining the substrate cavity; replacement with alanine reduces steric/aromatic interactions.
No new evidence this round; retained as a bulky-aromatic substitution candidate with potential to disrupt substrate binding.
Pathogenic prediction (0.635) supports LOF; moderate MSA (0.095) provides marginal viability evidence, though ESM is near zero. Kept in top-3 due to phenotype relevance.
Phenotype 0.635 and decent evolutionary support; annotation adds nothing but does not reduce confidence.
Tyrosine 220 near W216 is likely part of the aromatic cage; removing the hydroxyl and aromatic ring should alter substrate recognition.
No new evidence this round; retained for aromatic side-chain disruption in a likely transport-relevant region.
Pathogenic prediction (0.756) supports transport ablation; low ESM and MSA reduce confidence but not enough to drop below top-3 given phenotype emphasis.
